proposals.before: Day guimao: Xiao Chao, newly made minister of education and prince of Poyang, and Xiao Zilong, prince of Suizhou and central-army general-in-chief, were put to death.
proposals.after: Day guiwei: Xiao Chao, newly made minister of education and prince of Poyang, and Xiao Zilong, prince of Suizhou and central-army general-in-chief, were put to death.
proposals.reason: Chinese 癸未 is guiwei, not guimao (癸卯).

proposals.before: Day guimao: the newly appointed Minister of Education Prince Chao of Poyang and Central-Army General-in-Chief Prince Zilong of Suizhou were executed.
proposals.after: Day guiwei: the newly appointed Minister of Education Prince Chao of Poyang and Central-Army General-in-Chief Prince Zilong of Suizhou were executed.
proposals.reason: Chinese 癸未 is guiwei, not guimao (癸卯).

proposals.before: Also killed were Xiao Rui, prince of Nanping and inspector of Xiangzhou; Xiao Chao, prince of Jinxi and inspector of Ying; and Xiao Keng, prince of Yidu and inspector of South Yuzhou.
proposals.after: Also killed were Xiao Rui, prince of Nanping and inspector of Xiangzhou; Xiao Qiu, prince of Jinxi and inspector of Ying; and Xiao Keng, prince of Yidu and inspector of South Yuzhou.
proposals.reason: Given name 銶 is Qiu, not Chao; Chao belongs to 鏘 (Prince of Poyang).

proposals.before: Also executed were Inspector of Xiangzhou Prince Rui of Nanping, Inspector of Yingzhou Prince Chao of Jinxi, and Inspector of South Yuzhou Prince Keng of Yidu.
proposals.after: Also executed were Inspector of Xiangzhou Prince Rui of Nanping, Inspector of Yingzhou Prince Qiu of Jinxi, and Inspector of South Yuzhou Prince Keng of Yidu.
proposals.reason: Given name 銶 is Qiu, not Chao; Chao belongs to 鏘 (Prince of Poyang).

decisions.reason: Chinese day graph 癸未 is the sexagenary day guiwei; the original English guimao corresponds to 癸卯 and is a real naming error. The proposed replacement corrects only that day name and otherwise matches the Chinese.
Chinese day graph 癸未 is guiwei, not guimao (癸卯); the literal field makes the same day-name error as the idiomatic, and the proposed fix restores the correct reading without other changes.

Chinese 晉熙王銶 names Prince Qiu of Jinxi; 銶 is Qiu, while Chao belongs to 鏘 (鄱陽王鏘) in s0028. The original idiomatic wrongly transfers Chao onto this prince, and the proposed Xiao Qiu is the accurate given-name reading.
Chinese 晉熙王銶 is Prince Qiu of Jinxi; the literal Prince Chao misreads 銶 as Chao (proper to 鏘). Replacing Chao with Qiu corrects the given name without altering the rest of the sentence.
